text: Act only on that maxim through which you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law.
author: Immanuel Kant
source: Groundwork for the Metaphysic of Morals

text: Act in such a way as to treat humanity, whether in your own person or in that of anyone else, always as an end and never merely as a means.
author: Immanuel Kant
source: Groundwork for the Metaphysic of Morals

text: I think, therefore I am.
author: René Descartes

text: What is rational is actual; and what is actual is rational.

source: Elements of the Philosophy of Right

text: One must still have chaos in oneself to be able to give birth to a dancing star.

text: He who fights with monsters should look to it that he himself does not become a monster.

text: The struggle itself toward the heights is enough to fill a man's heart.

text: There is no fate that cannot be surmounted by scorn.

text: To will oneself moral and to will oneself free are one and the same decision.

text: The curious paradox is that when I accept myself just as I am, then I can change.

text: Do I contradict myself? / Very well then I contradict myself, / (I am large, I contain multitudes.)

source: Song of Myself, Leaves of Grass

text: Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

author: G. W. Leibniz
source: Principles of Nature and Grace, Based on Reason

text: Inside and outside are inseparable. The world is wholly inside and I am wholly outside myself.

text: Some things are in our control and others not.

text: Anxiety is the dizziness of freedom.

text: The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao.

text: You cannot go into the same water twice.

text: That thou art, O Śvetaketu.
author: Chandogya Upanishad

text: Never did eye see the sun unless it had first become sunlike.
author: Plotinus

text: The self is a relation which relates itself to its own self.
author: Søren Kierkegaard

author: Karl Jaspers

author: Jean-Paul Sartre

author: Alfred North Whitehead

text: Faith is to accept oneself as accepted.
author: Paul Tillich
